data.narrative:
Rangeview is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Cameron Schiller and Aeden Gasser-Brennan, having raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ) within the Robotics & Manufacturing sector.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and anchors the analysis. Using the $5M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, this method implies a $12M post-money valuation. Peer-median analysis is not applicable: while 10 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters required (matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) yielded fewer than three datapoints, making a peer-derived multiple unreliable and an all-sector median potentially misleading.

The triangulation range is $11M to $14M, with a median of $12M. This estimate carries material uncertainty given reliance on a single method and the absence of sufficient narrow comparables. Key risks include the nascency of the comp set in this segment, execution risk at the Seed stage, and sensitivity to market conditions for robotics and manufacturing automation. Additional comparable data at the Seed or Series A stage would strengthen conviction in this range.
